We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}) & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=6\sqrt{x} & \,⟹\,v=\int 6\sqrt{x}\,dx=4{x}^{3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}6\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})(4{x}^{3/2}){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}(4{x}^{3/2})(\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[4{e}^{3/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-4(1)^{3/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡((1)^{2})]-8{\int }_{1}^{e}{x}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{e}^{3/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-\frac{16{x}^{3/2}}{3}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{4}} \\  & =8{e}^{3/2}-(\frac{16{e}^{3/2}}{3}-\frac{16}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(24{e}^{3/2}-16{e}^{3/2}+16) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(8{e}^{3/2}+16) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}({e}^{3/2}+2).\end{aligned}
$$
